## **5\. Non-Functional Requirements** {#5.-non-functional-requirements}

This section specifies the non-functional requirements that govern how CareBridge must operate across the Mobile App, Expert Portal, Admin & Moderation Portal, Partner Portal, backend services and external integrations. These requirements apply to all functional requirements, workflows, screens and business rules unless a stricter requirement is defined in a specific use case.

### **5.1 External Interfaces** {#5.1-external-interfaces}

CareBridge communicates with human users, mobile device capabilities, web browsers and external software services. All interfaces must enforce role-based access control, explicit consent, auditability and healthcare-safety boundaries defined in the functional specification and appendix.

#### ***5.1.1 User Interfaces*** {#5.1.1-user-interfaces}

* **NFR-UI-01:** The mobile app must support Mother, Family Member/Caregiver and Verified Expert workflows through responsive screens for account setup, care journey tracking, community Q\&A, AI triage, emergency map, consultation, family sync, connected devices, pregnancy exercise and safety monitoring.

* **NFR-UI-02:** The web portals must support Verified Expert, System Admin, Moderator, Content Admin and Partner Representative workflows through role-specific dashboards, queues, detail screens, configuration screens and audit views.

* **NFR-UI-03:** All screens that collect sensitive health, location, payment or identity data must display clear validation, confirmation or safety messages before the user submits or shares the data.

* **NFR-UI-04:** Safety-critical outputs, including AI triage, emergency alerts, fall-detection events, nearby-care guidance and consultation boundaries, must be visually distinguishable from normal informational messages.

#### ***5.1.2 Software and Service Interfaces*** {#5.1.2-software-and-service-interfaces}

* **NFR-SI-01:** The backend must expose secure APIs for mobile and web clients using authenticated requests, role checks, consent checks and request validation before processing protected data.

* **NFR-SI-02:** VNPay payment integration must support consultation fee payment, payment status callback, commission calculation, dispute/refund tracing and reconciliation without exposing raw card or bank credentials to CareBridge.

* **NFR-SI-03:** Firebase Cloud Messaging or an equivalent notification service must support reminder, community, consultation, moderation, emergency and family-alert notifications with retry and delivery-state logging.

* **NFR-SI-04:** TrackAsia Map Service must support nearby facility search, distance calculation, ETA, route display and location-based emergency or nearby-expert workflows only after location permission is granted.

* **NFR-SI-05:** Gemini AI Service and the RAG knowledge service must support symptom-intake structuring, safe guidance generation and verified-content retrieval while preserving disclaimers that the system does not diagnose, prescribe or replace emergency care.

* **NFR-SI-06:** ZegoCloud and Firebase Realtime services must support chat, voice, video or realtime consultation sessions for authorized participants and must expose connection status, session errors and termination events to the application.

* **NFR-SI-07:** The audit/security log interface must record consent changes, expert access, payment/refund events, admin actions, moderation actions, AI/safety events and security incidents in an immutable or tamper-evident manner.

#### ***5.1.3 Hardware, Device and Sensor Interfaces*** {#5.1.3-hardware,-device-and-sensor-interfaces}

* **NFR-DI-01:** Health device and smartwatch integrations must collect only user-approved data types, such as heart rate, steps, sleep, activity or related health trend data, and must allow users to disconnect the device and stop future sync.

* **NFR-DI-02:** Phone IMU sensor access for smart activity monitoring and fall-detection support must be permission-based, configurable and disableable by the user.

* **NFR-DI-03:** Camera access for MediaPipe posture analysis must be requested only during pregnancy exercise posture-check workflows and must not be used for unrelated background monitoring.

* **NFR-DI-04:** When sensor, wearable, camera or location permission is denied, unavailable or interrupted, the system must provide a graceful fallback such as manual input, limited-mode guidance or an explanatory message.

#### ***5.1.4 Communication Interfaces*** {#5.1.4-communication-interfaces}

* **NFR-CI-01:** All client-server and server-service communication that carries account, health, consultation, payment, location or audit data must use encrypted transport such as HTTPS/TLS.

* **NFR-CI-02:** External-service requests must include timeout handling, retry where appropriate and safe degradation so that third-party failures do not corrupt CareBridge data or bypass safety rules.

* **NFR-CI-03:** The system must record integration errors with correlation information sufficient for troubleshooting while avoiding exposure of sensitive health, payment or authentication secrets in logs.

### **5.2 Quality Attributes** {#5.2-quality-attributes}

The following quality attributes define measurable expectations for usability, reliability, performance, security, safety, maintainability, scalability, compatibility and data quality. They are mandatory acceptance criteria for CareBridge implementation and testing.

#### ***5.2.1 Usability*** {#5.2.1-usability}

* **NFR-US-01:** A first-time Mother user must be able to register, verify OTP, set up a basic journey profile and reach the home dashboard within 10 minutes without staff assistance under normal network conditions.

* **NFR-US-02:** A returning user must be able to log in, view today tasks/reminders, view notifications and open a care record within 3 minutes.

* **NFR-US-03:** A Family Member/Caregiver must be able to accept an invitation, view shared care information and complete an assigned task within 5 minutes after receiving the invitation.

* **NFR-US-04:** A Verified Expert must be able to update availability, view a consultation request and open the shared health summary within 5 minutes after login.

* **NFR-US-05:** Admin, moderator and content users must be able to process normal queue items using consistent list, filter, detail, decision and confirmation patterns across all web portals.

* **NFR-US-06:** All forms must provide field-level validation messages, preserve user-entered data after recoverable errors and clearly distinguish required fields from optional fields.

* **NFR-US-07:** The system must provide Vietnamese UI text for end users and may provide English labels where required by academic documentation, admin operation or external-service terminology.

* **NFR-US-08:** Destructive or sensitive actions such as deleting accounts, revoking permissions, disconnecting devices, cancelling consultation, refund decision, suspending users or sending emergency alerts must require confirmation before execution.

#### ***5.2.2 Reliability*** {#5.2.2-reliability}

* **NFR-RL-01:** Core authenticated functions, including login, profile access, care records, reminders, community feed, expert directory and notifications, must target at least 99.5% monthly availability during the pilot period, excluding scheduled maintenance.

* **NFR-RL-02:** Safety-related functions, including emergency alert creation, emergency map opening, family alert delivery attempt and safety-monitoring event recording, must target at least 99.9% monthly backend availability during the pilot period.

* **NFR-RL-03:** Planned maintenance should be scheduled during low-traffic hours and announced to affected users at least 24 hours in advance when user-facing downtime is expected.

* **NFR-RL-04:** Mean Time To Repair for critical production incidents affecting login, health record access, emergency alert processing or consultation payment should not exceed 4 hours during the pilot support window.

* **NFR-RL-05:** The system must prevent loss of confirmed user-created records after successful save, including health logs, baby logs, vaccination records, growth measurements, community posts, expert answers, consultation summaries and payment/refund records.

* **NFR-RL-06:** Notification, AI, map, payment, realtime and device-sync failures must be captured as recoverable errors with user-safe messages and retry/reconciliation paths where applicable.

* **NFR-RL-07:** Critical defects are defined as defects that cause unauthorized data disclosure, complete loss of confirmed data, inability to access emergency/safety functions, incorrect payment settlement, or inability for major roles to perform their primary workflow.

* **NFR-RL-08:** No release candidate may contain known unresolved critical defects; significant defects must have approved workaround or deferral records before pilot release.

#### ***5.2.3 Performance*** {#5.2.3-performance}

* **NFR-PF-01:** Under normal pilot load, 95% of authenticated API requests for standard create, read, update and delete operations must complete within 2 seconds, excluding third-party service latency.

* **NFR-PF-02:** Login, OTP verification and session refresh must complete within 3 seconds for 95% of successful requests under normal network conditions.

* **NFR-PF-03:** List screens such as community feed, notifications, consultation list, expert directory, moderation queue and admin user list must render the first page of results within 3 seconds for 95% of requests.

* **NFR-PF-04:** AI symptom-intake structuring and RAG answer generation should return an initial result within 10 seconds for 95% of requests; if processing takes longer, the UI must show progress or retry guidance.

* **NFR-PF-05:** Emergency map, nearby-care search, nearby-expert search and route/ETA calculation should return usable results within 5 seconds for 95% of requests when the map service is available.

* **NFR-PF-06:** Push notification delivery must be attempted within 30 seconds after the triggering backend event for reminders, consultation updates, moderation results and family alerts.

* **NFR-PF-07:** Realtime consultation connection setup for chat, voice or video should complete within 10 seconds for 95% of attempts when the realtime service and user network are available.

* **NFR-PF-08:** Health device sync should process newly available device data within 5 minutes of a scheduled sync cycle or within 30 seconds for a user-triggered manual sync, excluding external device-platform delay.

* **NFR-PF-09:** The pilot deployment must support at least 1,000 registered users, 200 daily active users, 50 verified experts, 20 partner representatives and 20 admin/moderation/content staff without architectural redesign.

#### ***5.2.4 Security and Privacy*** {#5.2.4-security-and-privacy}

* **NFR-SP-01:** The system must enforce authentication, role-based authorization and consent checks before allowing access to personal, health, family, consultation, payment, location or moderation data.

* **NFR-SP-02:** Sensitive data must be protected in transit with TLS and protected at rest using database, storage or platform-level encryption appropriate to the deployment environment.

* **NFR-SP-03:** Passwords must never be stored in plain text and must be protected using secure hashing and salting mechanisms.

* **NFR-SP-04:** OTP, access token and refresh session mechanisms must enforce expiration, retry limits, session revocation and suspicious-activity logging.

* **NFR-SP-05:** Users must be able to grant, view, limit and revoke data-sharing permissions for family members and experts where applicable; revocation must block future access except for legally or operationally retained records.

* **NFR-SP-06:** Location, camera, motion-sensor and device-health data must be collected only after explicit permission and only for the declared feature purpose.

* **NFR-SP-07:** Audit logs must record security-relevant events, admin actions, consent events, expert access, payment/refund actions, safety events and incident handling without exposing unnecessary sensitive payloads.

* **NFR-SP-08:** Account deletion and deactivation must follow retention notices for audit, financial, medical-record, investigation or legal-safety constraints defined by the appendix and business rules.

#### ***5.2.5 Safety and Compliance*** {#5.2.5-safety-and-compliance}

* **NFR-SF-01:** CareBridge must consistently present itself as a healthcare support platform, not a hospital, diagnosis system, prescription system or emergency medical service.

* **NFR-SF-02:** AI-generated and RAG-generated outputs must include safety boundaries, red-flag escalation guidance and instructions to seek professional or emergency care when risk indicators are detected.

* **NFR-SF-03:** Community answers and expert answers must be distinguishable, and user-generated community content must not be presented as verified medical advice.

* **NFR-SF-04:** Pregnancy exercise, posture analysis, growth tracking, vaccination reminders, AI triage and device trends must be framed as supportive guidance and tracking, not treatment decisions.

* **NFR-SF-05:** Emergency, fall-detection and nearby-support workflows must prioritize fast access to call, navigation, family alert and emergency instruction actions over non-critical content.

* **NFR-SF-06:** Moderation and abuse-prevention workflows must allow staff to hide unsafe content, resolve reports, warn or suspend accounts and escalate safety cases according to role permission.

#### ***5.2.6 Maintainability and Supportability*** {#5.2.6-maintainability-and-supportability}

* **NFR-MT-01:** Functional modules must be organized around the documented domains: account/access, mother and baby care, community, expert consultation, AI/RAG, reminders, family sync, partner governance, safety monitoring, content, moderation, payment and audit.

* **NFR-MT-02:** External integrations must be isolated behind service adapters so that mock, sandbox or replacement services can be used during academic testing or third-party outage.

* **NFR-MT-03:** Configuration for AI safety rules, consultation price bands, posture analysis, content categories, notification templates and moderation rules must be manageable without code changes where the functional specification defines admin screens.

* **NFR-MT-04:** Logs and monitoring must provide enough information to trace a failed request across client, backend and third-party service boundaries using correlation identifiers.

* **NFR-MT-05:** The system must maintain traceability between major features, use cases, screens, business rules and test cases so requirement changes can be reviewed safely.

#### ***5.2.7 Scalability and Capacity*** {#5.2.7-scalability-and-capacity}

* **NFR-SC-01:** The system architecture must allow horizontal scaling of backend APIs, notification workers, AI/RAG processing workers and realtime-session coordination components when user volume increases.

* **NFR-SC-02:** Data storage must support growth in health records, baby logs, community content, notifications, audit logs, uploaded files, consultation summaries and device-sync data without requiring changes to user workflows.

* **NFR-SC-03:** Search, filter and queue screens must use pagination or equivalent lazy loading to avoid loading unbounded records into the client.

* **NFR-SC-04:** The MVP must support Hanoi-first pilot operation and leave room for later national scaling without depending on nationwide healthcare database integration in the pilot scope.

#### ***5.2.8 Compatibility and Portability*** {#5.2.8-compatibility-and-portability}

* **NFR-CP-01:** Mobile functions must support commonly used modern Android and iOS devices capable of running the selected development framework, camera access, push notification and standard permission prompts.

* **NFR-CP-02:** Web portals must support current versions of Chrome, Edge and Safari on desktop or laptop screen sizes used by experts, administrators, moderators, content admins and partner representatives.

* **NFR-CP-03:** The UI must remain usable on common mobile screen sizes and must not require landscape orientation for normal mother, family or expert mobile workflows except where camera/posture workflow explicitly benefits from it.

* **NFR-CP-04:** If a third-party service is unavailable in a local development or demo environment, the system must support sandbox, mock or manual fallback behavior sufficient to demonstrate the related workflow safely.

#### ***5.2.9 Data Quality, Integrity and Auditability*** {#5.2.9-data-quality,-integrity-and-auditability}

* **NFR-DQ-01:** The system must validate required fields, data type, range and ownership before saving account, health, baby, vaccination, growth, payment, consultation, community, partner or safety records.

* **NFR-DQ-02:** Health trends, growth charts, vaccination schedules, device data and AI/RAG context must identify data sources where relevant, such as user-entered, expert-created, device-synced, imported or system-generated.

* **NFR-DQ-03:** The system must prevent duplicate processing of payment callbacks, notification jobs, device-sync events and emergency/safety events where duplicate processing could mislead users or corrupt records.

* **NFR-DQ-04:** Important records must keep created time, updated time, actor identity and status history where needed for audit, dispute, moderation, expert verification, consent or safety investigation.

* **NFR-DQ-05:** Reports and dashboards must use consistent definitions for active users, verified experts, contribution points, consultation revenue, commission, partner performance, safety events and impact metrics.

## **6\. Requirement Appendix** {#6.-requirement-appendix}

This appendix defines the cross-module business rules, common requirements, reusable application messages and additional constraints that govern the CareBridge system. These items are derived from the CareBridge use cases, context diagrams and main workflow diagrams. They are not independent use cases; they constrain how use cases, screens, services and background processes must behave. 

The rules in this appendix apply unless a more specific use case or functional requirement defines a stricter behavior.

### **6.1 Business Rules** {#6.1-business-rules}

Business rules define mandatory conditions and constraints that must be enforced by the CareBridge application, backend services and supporting integrations. Each rule includes traceability to the relevant use case group or workflow

#### ***6.1.1 Account, Identity, Role, and Access Control*** {#6.1.1-account,-identity,-role,-and-access-control}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-01 |  Role-Based Access Control | Before running any protected function, the backend must verify identity, active session, account status, role and permission scope. Hiding a UI control is not sufficient authorization. |
| BR-02 |  Actor Generalization | Mother, Family Member, Verified Expert, Moderator, Content Admin, Admin and Partner Representative inherit common User functions, but each role may access only role-specific functions assigned to it. |
| BR-03 | Protected Function Authentication | The system must block protected functions when the user is not logged in, the session has expired, or the account is blocked, suspended, deactivated or deleted. |
| BR-04 | OTP and Identity Re-verification | The system must re-verify identity before sensitive actions such as registration verification, password reset, password change, account deletion, role-sensitive changes and payment-sensitive decisions. |
| BR-05 | Session Lifecycle | A successful login creates an active session. Logout, account deactivation, password reset and session revocation must invalidate affected sessions or tokens immediately. |
| BR-06 | Account State Separation | Account deactivation and deletion are different states. Deactivation blocks normal use while preserving the account; deletion starts controlled removal subject to verification, retention, audit and dispute rules. |
| BR-07 | Administrative Role Management | Only authorized Admin users may create staff accounts, assign roles, change permissions or restrict accounts. The system must prevent privilege escalation outside the approved role model. |
| BR-08 | Sensitive Action Audit | The system must record audit events for password changes, session revocation, permission changes, health-data access, moderation, expert verification, payment/refund decisions, partner approval, safety alerts and security investigation. |

**Table 555: Account, Identity, Role, and Access Control Business Rules**

#### ***6.1.2 Privacy, Consent, Health Data, and***  {#6.1.2-privacy,-consent,-health-data,-and}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-09 | Data Ownership and Source Label | Each mother record, baby record, health summary, uploaded file, device metric, expert note, verified content item and partner item must retain the owner and source label where relevant. |
| BR-10 | Consent Attributes | Every sharing permission must store owner, recipient, purpose, allowed data scope, start time, expiry time and status. |
| BR-11 | Consent Expiry and Revocation | When permission expires or is revoked, the recipient must immediately lose future access. Required audit evidence may still be retained according to retention rules. |
| BR-12 | Sharing History | The system must keep a reviewable history of grant, update, expiry and revoke events so the data owner can see who had access, what was shared and when. |
| BR-13 | Privacy by Default | Health information, baby information, consultation data, exact location, online status, safety events and device metrics must be private by default. |
| BR-14 | Family Permission Granularity | Joining a care group does not provide full access. Family Members may view or update only data, tasks, reminders or alerts explicitly shared by the Mother. |
| BR-15 | Expert Access to Shared Data | Verified Expert status does not automatically grant access to personal health data. Experts may view only shared summaries or records within approved purpose, scope and validity period. |
| BR-16 | File Ownership and Authorized Access | Before upload, preview, download, archive or deletion, the system must check file ownership, linked record, current consent and access scope. |
| BR-17 | Archive and Soft Delete | The system should archive or soft-delete data instead of physical deletion when the data is tied to consultation, audit, investigation, payment, dispute or retention requirements. |
| BR-18 | Minimum Necessary Disclosure | Family alerts, nearby-support requests, dashboards, partner reports and impact reports must disclose only the minimum necessary data for the current purpose |

**Table 556: Privacy, Consent, Health Data, and Uploaded Medical Documents**

#### ***6.1.3 Community, Moderation, Content, and Partner Governance*** {#6.1.3-community,-moderation,-content,-and-partner-governance}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-19 | Community Content Ownership | Posts and answers from normal users must be treated as personal experience or emotional support. The system must not present them as diagnosis, treatment, prescription, dosage instruction, or emergency advice. |
| BR-20 | Anonymous Display Boundary | Anonymous mode hides the display identity from normal community viewers but does not hide the author from authorized moderation, audit and safety processes. |
| BR-21 | Community Safety Pre-check | Before publishing or routing community content, the system must check spam, prohibited content, unsafe keywords and red-flag health risk. |
| BR-22 | Red-Flag Community Routing | Potential emergency, self-harm, severe symptom or unsafe-care content must be routed to AI triage or emergency guidance before normal community discussion or paid consultation promotion. |
| BR-23 | Moderation Decision Governance | Moderators may approve, hide, reject, warn, restrict or suspend according to reason codes and audit policy. Users must receive clear status or rejection messages when applicable. |
| BR-24 | Verified Expert Answer Identification | Answers must be labeled as **Verified Expert Answers** only when the author is a verified expert and the expert status is valid for the answer context. The system must not display ordinary user answers, AI responses or partner content as verified expert answers. |
| BR-25 | Accepted Answer and Correctness Boundary | A question owner or authorized moderation process may mark an expert answer as accepted, helpful or selected. This marker means the answer was selected for the question context; it must not be presented as guaranteed medical correctness, diagnosis or prescription. |
| BR-26 | Verified Content Versioning | Articles, FAQs, checklists and exercise content must have category, version, status, reviewer and publication state. Only approved versions may be published or indexed for RAG. |
| BR-27 | Outdated or Unsafe Content Handling | Reported outdated, misleading or unsafe verified content must be reviewed and may be revised, unpublished and de-indexed from AI/RAG knowledge. |
| BR-28 | Partner and Sponsored Content Labeling | Partner clinic/service listings and sponsored content must be reviewed before publication and clearly labeled as partner or sponsored content. |

**Table 557: Community, Moderation, Content, and Partner Governance**

#### ***6.1.4 Expert Verification, Booking, Consultation, Payment, Pricing, Dispute, Refund, and Realtime Communication***  {#6.1.4-expert-verification,-booking,-consultation,-payment,-pricing,-dispute,-refund,-and-realtime-communication}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-29 | Expert Verification Before Practice | An expert must not appear as verified or provide official consultation until profile, credentials and required documents are approved by authorized admin users. |
| BR-30 | Expert Status Enforcement | Expired, rejected, suspended, revoked or unverified experts must be hidden from booking, nearby expert display and expert-answer routing. |
| BR-31 | Availability and Booking Consistency | Booking must use current expert availability and prevent double booking, invalid time slots and booking with ineligible experts. |
| BR-32 | Consultation Data Sharing Consent | Before consultation, the system must check whether the user has shared the selected health summary or records with the expert and must not expose unshared data. |
| BR-33 | Payment-Gated Booking State | A paid consultation must not be confirmed until payment status is successful or otherwise explicitly approved by a controlled rule. Failed, expired or cancelled payments must not create active consultations. |
| BR-34 | Refund, Dispute and No-show Governance | Cancellation, no-show, dispute and refund decisions must follow time, status, evidence and payment rules and must be auditable. |
| BR-35 | Commission Calculation | Expert revenue and platform commission must be calculated from completed eligible consultations according to the active commission configuration and refund state. |
| BR-36 | Consultation Pricing Control | Experts may set or update prices only within admin-configured price bands. Mothers must see the current consultation price before booking or payment. |
| BR-37 | Realtime Communication Eligibility | Chat, voice call or video call must be opened only for eligible consultation, support or approved contact contexts and must respect account, role, status and privacy rules. |
| BR-38 | Consultation Summary Boundary | Consultation summaries must be created by authorized experts and shown only to eligible users within the consultation context. They are support notes, not diagnosis or prescription. |

**Table 558: Expert Verification, Booking, Consultation, Payment, Pricing, Dispute, Refund,and Realtime Communication**

#### ***6.1.5 AI, Health Guidance, Exercise, Growth, and Reminder Safety*** {#6.1.5-ai,-health-guidance,-exercise,-growth,-and-reminder-safety}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-39 | AI Safety Boundary | AI/RAG/Triage output must be presented as support guidance only. It must not diagnose, prescribe, replace doctors, replace hospitals or delay emergency/offline care. |
| BR-40 | Red-Flag Overrides Normal Flow | When red-flag indicators are detected, emergency guidance, nearby care and safe action must take priority over community posting, self-care tips or paid consultation promotion. |
| BR-41 | AI Input Scope Control | AI intake may use only the symptom text, selected records, device data or RAG sources that the user has approved for that interaction. |
| BR-42 | AI Fallback and Escalation | If AI service is unavailable, incomplete or unsafe, the system must show fallback guidance and safe next actions without fabricating medical advice. |
| BR-43 | Exercise Safety Pre-check | Pregnancy exercise sessions must require safety disclaimer and contraindication checklist before starting. Failed safety checks must block the exercise session and advise offline care when needed. |
| BR-44 | Posture Feedback Boundary | MediaPipe posture feedback must be treated as exercise-form assistance only, not medical assessment. Low camera quality must trigger retry, reposition or continue-without-posture options. |
| BR-45 | Growth and Health Trend Disclaimer | Growth charts, health metrics and device trends provide tracking and visualization only. Abnormal values should trigger guidance to consult experts or offline care, not diagnosis. |
| BR-46 | Reminder and Checklist Safety | Reminders and checklists must not override urgent care guidance. Missed reminders should be visible but must not imply medical failure or emergency status unless connected to a safety workflow. |
| BR-47 | Health Content Source Control | Health guidance, checklist, FAQ and exercise instructions must use approved content sources and show appropriate safety wording when used in app, AI/RAG or expert workflows. |

**Table 559: AI, Health Guidance, Exercise, Growth, and Reminder Safety**

#### ***6.1.6 Map, Location, Nearby Support, and Connected Devices*** {#6.1.6-map,-location,-nearby-support,-and-connected-devices}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-48 | Location Permission Requirement | Exact user or expert location may be collected or shared only after explicit location permission and purpose-specific consent. |
| BR-49 | Manual Location Fallback | If location permission is denied or unavailable, emergency and nearby-care workflows must provide manual location entry, quick call or default safety guidance. |
| BR-50 | Map Service Boundary | Map, route, distance and ETA results are guidance only. CareBridge must not guarantee ambulance dispatch, facility availability or medical response. |
| BR-51 | Nearby Expert Opt-in | Experts appear in nearby-support results only if verified, eligible, currently opted in and within configured radius, duration and visibility scope. |
| BR-52 | Nearby Request Minimum Data | Nearby support requests must share only minimum necessary request data until an expert accepts, rejects, expires or the requester cancels the request. |
| BR-53 | No Sponsored Blocking Before Safe Action | Emergency and red-flag workflows must not place ads, sponsored content or partner promotion before safe action options such as emergency guidance, nearby care or quick call. |
| BR-54 | Connected Device Consent and Scope | Smartwatch or wearable data import must explain data types, sync frequency, source labels, retention and limitations before connection or manual import. |
| BR-55 | Device Data Quality Rules | Missing, stale, duplicated or conflicting device data must be labeled and must not be fabricated, silently overwritten or used as confirmed medical evidence. |

**Table 560: Map, Location, Nearby Support, and Connected Devices**

#### ***6.1.7 Smart Activity Monitoring and Safety Support (MF21)*** {#6.1.7-smart-activity-monitoring-and-safety-support-(mf21)}

| ID | Business Rule  | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-56 | Voluntary Activation | MF-21 must be off by default. It may start only after the Mother reads the limitations, gives the required permissions, completes the safety settings, and confirms consent. Sharing location remains optional. |
| BR-57 | Sensor and Background Limitation | The system must not promise that MF-21 will run continuously on every phone. Where practical, raw motion data should be processed on the device and should not be uploaded continuously unless there is a clear need and valid consent. |
| BR-58 | Suspected Event Wording | Motion analysis may create only a “suspected fall/impact” event. The system must not say that the user is injured, unconscious, or definitely in an emergency. |
| BR-59 | Mandatory Safety Check | After detecting a suspected event, the system must open the safety-check screen with sound, vibration, and a countdown. The user must be able to select “I am safe”, “Need help”, or “Emergency support”. |
| BR-60 | Family Alert Conditions | The system may send a family alert only when the Mother selects “Need help” or does not respond before the countdown ends. The alert may go only to configured contacts and may include location only when permission exists. |
| BR-61 | Safety History and False Positives | The system must keep the minimum event details and the user's response in safety history. The user may mark an event as a false positive, but the original sensor-event information and any alert already sent must not be rewritten. |
| BR-62 | MF-21 to MF-19 Escalation | MF-21 may open the MF-19 emergency-support flow so the user can call, search for nearby care, or start navigation. This action does not dispatch an ambulance or guarantee that help will arrive. |

**Table 561: Smart Activity Monitoring and Safety Support**

### **6.2 Common Requirements** {#6.2-common-requirements}

This section specifies common requirements shared across multiple modules. They support consistent behavior for authentication, authorization, validation, privacy, external-service interaction, safety handling, auditing and traceability.

| ID | Common Request | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| CR-01 | Authentication Check | Every protected UI action, API endpoint and background action must verify the current session and account state before execution. |
| CR-02 | Authorization Check | Authorization must be enforced server-side using role, ownership, consent and feature permission checks. |
| CR-03 | Input Validation | All user input, upload metadata, payment status, location values and external-service responses must be validated before storage or use. |
| CR-04 | Error Handling | The system must show safe, user-understandable errors without exposing internal stack traces, tokens or sensitive data. |
| CR-05 | Audit Event Creation | Sensitive actions must create append-only audit events with actor, action, target, timestamp, result and reason where applicable. |
| CR-06 | Consent Gate | Any access to shared health data, location, device metrics, consultation summary or safety alert must pass active consent and scope checks. |
| CR-07 | Notification Preference Handling | Noncritical notifications must respect user preferences. Safety-critical notifications may follow special mandatory-delivery rules. |
| CR-08 | External Service Fallback | If payment, AI, map, notification, realtime or storage services fail, the system must show a safe fallback state and preserve data consistency. |
| CR-09 | Traceability | Each rule, message and common requirement should be traceable to at least one UC group or workflow section. |
| CR-10 | Data Minimization | Only collect, display and transmit the minimum data needed for the active use case and purpose. |
| CR-11 | Source and Timestamp Labeling | Records imported from device, uploaded by user, generated by expert or created by system must include source and timestamp when relevant. |
| CR-12 | Status Consistency | State changes such as pending, approved, rejected, cancelled, expired, completed, refunded, suspended and revoked must be consistent across UI and backend. |
| CR-13 | Idempotency for Sensitive Actions | Payment confirmation, refund, notification retry, device sync retry and alert delivery retry must avoid duplicate side effects. |
| CR-14 | Retention and Deletion | Deletion, archive, anonymization and retention must preserve required audit, dispute and safety evidence while honoring privacy requirements. |
| CR-15 | Localization | User-facing messages should support approved Vietnamese wording while preserving message codes and safety meaning. |
| CR-16 | Accessibility and Readability | Critical safety, consent, payment and error messages must be visible, readable and not hidden behind decorative content. |
| CR-17 | Versioned Content | Verified content, exercise configuration, AI/RAG knowledge and safety wording must be version-controlled and auditable. |
| CR-18 | Role-specific Navigation | Users must be routed to the correct dashboard and feature set after login based on role and onboarding state. |
| CR-19 | Sensitive Data Masking | OTP targets, contact details, health data previews and dashboard indicators must be masked or summarized when full display is not authorized. |
| CR-20 | Safe Default State | When the system cannot verify permission, service response, expert status or safety state, it must default to the safer restrictive behavior. |
| CR-21 | No Fabricated Results | The system must not fabricate payment confirmation, AI output, device metrics, location ETA or notification delivery status when an external service fails. |
| CR-22 | Report Consistency | Section 6 business rules, messages and common requirements must remain consistent with context diagrams, workflows, use case list and functional requirements. |

**Table 562: Common Requirements**

### **6.3 Application Messages List** {#6.3-application-messages-list}

This section defines reusable, safety-critical, and cross-module messages. The UI may provide approved Vietnamese translations, but the message code, severity and safety meaning must remain unchanged. Function-specific success messages may be added in screen specifications.

Message type and display color convention used in this section:

1. Inline message (neutral/dark gray or red when blocking): text displayed inside the screen area near the related content or action.

2. Inline red under field: validation text displayed in red under or near an input field; the related input may also use a red border until corrected.

3. Toast message (green/blue/red): temporary feedback displayed after an action; green indicates success, blue indicates neutral information and red indicates failure.

4. Confirmation dialog (neutral or red destructive action): a dialog that asks the user to confirm a sensitive or irreversible action before continuing.

5. Modal dialog (neutral/amber/red): a blocking dialog used when the user must read or resolve the message before continuing; amber/red may be used for warning or safety-critical cases.

6. Banner / safety notice (amber or red): a persistent and visible notice; amber is used for caution/limitation and red is used for urgent, emergency or safety-critical action.

7. Badge / label (blue/green/amber/gray): a short visual label; blue or green identifies verified content/expert answers, amber identifies accepted or selected answers, and gray identifies partner or sponsored content. 

#### ***6.3.1 Common Validation and Access Messages*** {#6.3.1-common-validation-and-access-messages}

| Message Code | Message Type | Context | Content |
| ----- | :---- | ----- | ----- |
| MSG-COM-01 | Toast message (red) | Authentication | Your session has expired. Please log in again to continue. |
| MSG-COM-02 | Inline message (red) | Authorization | You do not have permission to perform this action or view this data. |
| MSG-COM-03 | Modal dialog (neutral) | Sensitive action | Please verify your identity before continuing this sensitive action. |
| MSG-COM-04 | Inline message (red) | Account state | This account is currently restricted, deactivated, suspended or deleted. |
| MSG-COM-05 | Toast message (green) | Logout/session | The selected session has been signed out successfully. |

### **6.4 Other Requirements** {#6.4-other-requirements}

Other cross-cutting constraints capture rules that must be stated in the SRS but should not be modeled as standalone use cases.

| ID | Requirement | Descrip |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| OR-01 | Safety Boundary | CareBridge is a maternal and early childhood health support platform, not a hospital information system, medical diagnosis tool, prescription system or emergency dispatch service. |
| OR-02 | No Diagnosis / No Prescription | No AI, expert summary, community answer, device trend, posture feedback or growth chart may be worded as official diagnosis or prescription. |
| OR-03 | Audit Immutability | Audit records must be append-only for normal operators. Corrections must be made by additional records, not by editing or deleting existing evidence. |
| OR-04 | Raw IMU Retention Limit | Continuous raw phone IMU streams must not be stored long term. Only suspected event metadata and safety confirmation results should be retained as required. |
| OR-05 | External Service Dependency | Payment, map, AI, notification, realtime, storage and health-device services are external dependencies and require fallback, retry and reconciliation handling. |
| OR-06 | Partner Transparency | Sponsored or partner-provided items must be labeled and must not be prioritized above safety actions in emergency or red-flag flows. |
| OR-07 | Data Protection | Encryption, access control, consent checks, source labels, retention rules and audit logging are security/data requirements, not separate end-user use cases. |
| OR-08 | Localization | Approved Vietnamese UI wording may be used, but message codes, severity and safety meaning must remain consistent. |
| OR-09 | Consistency with Diagrams | Business rules must stay consistent with the Web/Mobile context diagrams and the 14 main workflow diagrams. |
| OR-10 | Consistency with Use Cases | Rules that UC guidance marks as cross-cutting must remain in Section 6 rather than being drawn as independent use cases. |

**Table 568: Other Requirements**
